items.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Uncle Ernie was playing with Benny Goodman.

ctx.x: I understand Buddy had a big impact on the – combining those.

Yeah. It took a while before they combined and made Local 47. It was different. It was the same thing with Rosemary’s Uncle Ernie. Uncle Ernie was playing with Benny Goodman. They wanted him to go – come and play with Duke [Ellington], but in order for him to play with Duke, he had to leave the white union and join the black union. He felt he was going to lose all his gigs, and so he couldn’t do it, because it was – in those days, it was always a black union and a white union.
